gloss: borrowed thing; something not one's own

definitions.gloss: borrowed thing; something not one's own
definitions.explanation: Something borrowed from someone else. Figuratively, ideas, words or a style taken over from others rather than one's own, often with a critical tone ({借|か}り{物|もの}の{言葉|ことば}, 'borrowed words').

examples.japanese: ⟦これ→これ：00963_kore⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{借|か}り{物|もの}です。
{借|か}り{物|もの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{傘|かさ}→傘：00639_kasa⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧なくしてしまった。
examples.english: I lost an umbrella I had borrowed.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{意見|いけん}→意見：01303_iken⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦どこか→どこか：02361_dokoka⟧{借|か}り{物|もの}で、⟦{本人|ほんにん}→本人：03627_honnin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{考|かんが}え→考え：00855_kangae⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えない→見える：01165_mieru⟧。
examples.english: His opinions sound borrowed somehow; you can't see what he himself thinks.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {借|か}り{物|もの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧: borrowed words, phrases that are not one's own
- {借|か}り{物|もの}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{思想|しそう}→思想：03173_shisou⟧: borrowed ideas
- {借|か}り{物|もの}⟦{競走|きょうそう}→競走：15644_kyousou⟧: a borrowing race (a school sports-day race in which runners must fetch an item named on a card)

USAGE:
In the figurative sense, calling someone's words or ideas {借|か}り{物|もの} criticizes them as secondhand and lacking conviction.
